name: Doji Sayaka
concept: She speaks in elaborate metaphors even when a direct answer would serve, turning simple questions into riddles that give her time to measure who is listening and what they want to hear, though it leaves people uncertain whether she is being evasive or simply cannot help herself anymore.

answers.giri: You must dismantle the Perfect Land Sect's influence before it unsettles the Crane, using honeyed words where others would wield steel, even as the mask you wear grows indistinguishable from your face.
answers.ninjo: You hunger to be known truly by another soul, even once, before you become merely the perfect performance that greets death's stage.
answers.standout_quality: You mastered the art of seeming ordinary, dissolving into crowds as easily as water takes the shape of any vessel, earning your Water ring's advancement through countless missions where invisibility proved more valuable than any blade.
answers.accomplishment: She identified a Perfect Land Sect recruiter operating from within the Doji household by watching how his eyes moved when servants spoke of the harvest, and reported him to her daimyō before he could sway anyone to the sect's cause.
answers.challenge: During her briefings with the daimyō, Sayaka sometimes cannot recall whether she witnessed the sect recruiter's movements herself or only heard them described, and must ask carefully neutral questions to reconstruct what she actually saw.
answers.peace: In the dusty archive rooms of the Doji household, she reconstructs the sect recruiter's movements by cross-referencing old ledgers and servant records, each verified detail settling the fog between what she witnessed and what she was told, until the past becomes solid ground beneath her.
answers.fear: Three days into arranging the sect recruiter's movements under house arrest, Sayaka realizes she cannot remember whether she ordered the guards herself or simply approved an order someone else had drafted, and the uncertainty keeps her in the Doji compound retracing every conversation instead of pursuing the network spreading through the merchant quarters.
answers.accoutrement: She wears a jade comb carved to look like layered water, which she takes from her hair and sets on the table during negotiations, though she never seems to notice when it goes missing and always has another one the next day.

clan_relationship.text:
# Clan Relationship: Doji

You find yourself drawn to a distant Doji cousin whose genuine warmth makes the performance exhausting rather than natural, and you must choose whether the Crane's demand for perfect grace permits you to lower your mask, even fractionally, with one of your own blood.

mentor.name: Yogo Morishige
mentor.text: Yogo Morishige taught her to trace a lie through what people choose not to say, but Sayaka has spent so long listening for absences that she sometimes cannot tell what she actually heard from what the silence suggested.

answers.first_impression: She speaks in elaborate metaphors even when a direct answer would serve, turning simple questions into riddles that give her time to measure who is listening and what they want to hear, though it leaves people uncertain whether she is being evasive or simply cannot help herself anymore.
answers.stress_reaction: When pushed past composure, Sayaka's hands go still—she stops adjusting her sleeves, stops touching the jade comb, stops the small precise movements that fill her silences—and speaks in direct sentences without metaphor until the moment passes.
answers.relationships:
Doji Kenzaburo (Crane) — Kenzaburo once asked her directly whether the metaphors were a choice or a habit, and she answered him in plain sentences for three minutes before reaching for the jade comb and never speaking that way to him again.
Otomo Koemi (Imperial) — Otomo Koemi caught her in the merchant quarter dressed as a laborer and said nothing about it to anyone, which means Sayaka must now decide whether to trust her or treat her as a threat that will eventually move.

parent_opinion.description: Her mother worries that Sayaka has perfected the art of answering without ever actually responding, and cannot tell anymore whether this is strategy or whether her daughter has simply forgotten how to say what she means.

answers.heritage: A Little Too Close to Heaven
answers.death: Sayaka dies in the archive room she loves, surrounded by ledgers and records, finally certain of what she witnessed and what she merely heard—and realizes in that moment of perfect clarity that she can no longer remember her own face without consulting a mirror.

bio:
Doji Sayaka is a refined diplomat serving the Doji daimyō, tasked with monitoring the Perfect Land Sect to ensure the Crane are not caught off guard. If necessary, she is expected to subtly undermine its leadership and cause its collapse. A master of diplomacy, she always speaks in extended metaphors, guiding conversations with elegance and intent.

She is impeccably dressed, maintaining an air of poise and control. She appears perfectly at ease with any outcome, rarely showing joy or displeasure, always maintaining a neutral mask. Despite this, she secretly struggles with sincerity, as her life has been one of perceptions and careful maneuvering, making true honesty difficult.

Sayaka occasionally disguises herself as a peasant, blending among the common folk to see the world from their eyes. Though she longs for genuine connection, she keeps others at a careful distance, fearing vulnerability. Deep down, she sees death as the final performance, believing that even in her last moments, she must meet her fate with grace and dignity.
